  "text": "The ironing board was still behind the pantry door, where Ruth had always kept it.

Daniel carried it into the kitchen. One leg caught on the frame.

“You have to turn it sideways,” his sister said.

“I remember.”

He turned it sideways.

They had come to empty the cupboards. By lunchtime they had filled one box with chipped plates and another with things neither wanted to throw away.

Clare plugged in the iron.

“What are you doing?”

She held up their mother’s blue tablecloth.

“It won’t fold properly.”

“It’s going in a bag.”

“I know where it’s going.”

Daniel sat down. There was a pale square on the wall where the calendar had hung. He had taken it down that morning, then put it in the box with the plates.

The iron clicked. Clare sprinkled water from a cup onto the cloth, dipping her fingers and shaking them over it.

“She had a bottle for that,” Daniel said.

“It broke.”

“When?”

“Christmas.”

He watched her work around a small brown mark.

“That won’t come out.”

“I’m not trying to get it out.”

Outside, the neighbour started his mower, stopped it, then started it again.

Clare lifted the finished end. Daniel stood to take it before it touched the floor. They held the cloth between them.

“Your way,” she said.

He brought his corners to hers. They folded it twice more, stepping closer each time.

“Will you take it?” she asked.

“My table’s round.”

“It’ll still cover it.”

He laid the folded cloth over his coat. Clare unplugged the iron and left it standing on the board to cool."
